title: Refactor stability sandbox notes
content:
Notes-to-self: quick brain dump for the large refactor (async-kv-cache) before merging to main. Want a short, reproducible runbook that I can hand to SREs/QA and to my future-self when this inevitably behaves oddly.

Background/context:
- Goal of refactor: decouple async KV cache lifecycle from request path; allow cache warming in background and make eviction policy pluggable.
- Risk areas: cache coherence during failovers, per-request latency tail spikes (cold cache), memory growth due to leak in background tasks, incorrect key TTL semantics across model variants.
- Repo: serving-runtime. Changes touch: cache manager, request router, trace/span annotations, config schema (yaml -> new cache policies).

Sandbox environment plan (cheap, repeatable):
1) Local docker-compose with tiny GPU shim (cpu-only mode) + instrumented workload generator. Use the same sequence-length distribution used in prod smoke tests (mix: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long).
2) Canary branch deploy via ephemeral k8s namespace (dev cluster): 2 pods running refactor branch, 2 pods running current main. Use weighted routing (10% to branch) to compare metrics side-by-side.
3) Synthetic golden prompts: pick 10 sequences that historically caused longest KV hits (long prefix reuse). Use both model-gpt2-medium-ish and gpt-j variants in the sandbox to validate different kv key derivations.
4) KV eviction worst-case: run continuous-high-churn workload to force eviction and ensure we don't regress correctness (no OOM/incorrect responses).

What to measure (minimal measurable set):
- P50/P95/P99 token latency per route (streaming enabled)
- Request CPU and GPU utilization per pod
- Memory RSS growth over 30m window (leak indicator)
- Number of background cache tasks active per node (should be stable)
- Error rate: 5xx, response mismatch to golden baseline (character-level diff > threshold)
- KV hit-rate and backend round trips per request
- Traces: ensure trace ids propagate from request -> background warmers -> cache manager

Smoke checklist before merging (quick gates):
- Unit tests: cache TTL semantics and eviction hooks added (pass locally and CI).
- Integration tests: 3 synthetic scenarios (cold-start, warm-run, eviction-churn) pass in CI-staging (flaky allowed once but must be <5% flakiness).
- Linting: config schema changes validated by schema-check tool (config-schema-ci).
- Canary metrics: after 1h of 10% traffic, P99 not worse than main by >15% and no >0.5% increase in errors.
- Memory: no >10% memory delta between branch and main at steady-state for 30m.
- Traces: background tasks show correct parent span and no orphaned spans.

Rollback plan (short):
- If P99 or errors exceed thresholds for >5 minutes after canary ramp, flip traffic back to main (automated CF script: infra/canary/revert.sh).
- If memory leak observed: scale down branch pods to 0 and open JIRA INF-1293 with dump and traces.
- Reproduce locally with same load pattern, capture heap profiles and run async task debugger.

Quick refactor follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add a metric to parse evicted-key reasons (LRU vs TTL vs manual) and expose via console Optimize tab.
- Hook a regression alert tied to a small eval set of golden prompts (automated daily eval, Slack bridge).
- Add small integration test that simulates cluster restart and validates cache warming resumes without duplicate warms.

Edge cases / unresolved questions (brain dump):
- Race around TTL update: if a request extends TTL while a background warmer is evicting the same key, we need compare-and-set semantics on TTL; current impl doesn't have CAS. Proposed quick fix: store update-ts and only evict if last-access < eviction-cutoff. Need to check DB semantics for persistent caches (redis).
- What happens to inflight requests when cache manager restarts? Should requests wait for warmers or fallback to model generation? Current idea: fallback to model generation + enqueue background warm (fail-open). Is this acceptable latency-wise for dedicated customers? Add a config flag: warm-blocking: true|false.
- Is it OK to log cache warm tasks at INFO? Might flood observability. Prefer debug with sampling.

Testing commands (local):
- ./scripts/run-local-smoke --profile=golden-prompts --workers=8 --duration=10m
- k top -n dev-ephemeral to watch mem/cpu
- curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/debug/heapdump -> attach to JIRA if >100MB growth

PR checklist additions (to PR template):
- "Sandbox runbook added to users/ (refactor-stability-sandbox-notes-<owner>.json)"
- "Canary policy documented and automated revert script linked"
- "Golden prompt bundle attached under testdata/golden/"
- "Console metrics names and trace changes documented in PR description"

Open TODOs (short):
- [ ] Finalize TTL CAS semantics with Priya (infra team) by 2025-11-07
- [ ] Add sampled debug logs to warmers (Maya)
- [ ] Wire eviction reason metric (Ethan)
- [ ] Run 24h sandbox run on dev cluster once merged to find leaks

Random notes / heuristics (for future refactors):
- Prefer fail-open for user-visible requests, but fail-fast for background maintenance tasks.
- Keep canary windows long enough to capture memory growth (>=30m); latency-only tests can be short (10m).
- Always attach a small set of deterministic inputs (golden prompts) to every refactor PR that touches inference path.

If anything goes sideways, ping @maya and @ethan on Slack and escalate to SRE on-call. This doc is intentionally rough — use as handoff for the first 24h after merge.

End of notes.
